notes.title: Every question checked against your notes
notes.html:
Quizzes, flashcards and mock exams no longer show a question your notes do not back. Before anything reaches you, Anvira finds the sentence in your notes that states its answer, checks that the sentence is about what the question asks, that the numbers agree, and that no other option is also right. Then the AI answers the question again without seeing the answer key; if it disagrees, the question is left out. "Which is NOT…" questions, options that contain the answer, and names or terms your notes never use are left out too.

Tested on 58 questions and cards written by the Qwen2.5-Coder 3B model and checked by hand: all 17 wrong or unfair ones were caught, and all 41 good ones were kept. Before this update, about a quarter of a mock exam's questions could be wrong.

  • You get the number of questions you asked for. A quiz of 25 sometimes came out with 5. Anvira now reads all of your material and, when the checks leave out questions, writes more from parts not asked about yet. If your notes really cannot support that many, it says so instead.
  • The answer comes from your notes. After each quiz answer and on the mock exam results you see "From your notes", with the sentence that proves it.

notes.title: Mock exams
notes.html:
• Choose the question types: Mixed (multiple choice, identification and written, in sections like a real exam), Multiple choice, Identification or Written.
  • Identification questions are new: write the term, name or number. Small spelling slips are accepted, and you can change a mark you disagree with.
  • Faster to make: each part of your notes is read once for all question types, and no more extra rounds to chase the last question or two.

notes.title: Cheat sheet and study guide cover every source
notes.html: Both used to read only the part of the notebook that best matched one search, so with 6 lessons they often covered only 2. Now every source is read and gets its own section, and lines your notes do not back are left out.

notes.title: Ask Pochi with many sources
notes.html: Notebook chat now handles 6 to 10 sources, even with small models. Pochi always knows which sources the notebook has and what each covers. A question about everything ("summarize all the lessons", "compare lesson 3 and 4") gets every lesson, and the passages it reads are cut down to the sentences that matter, so more fits in the same space. Tested on a 10-source notebook: the passage with the answer was included for 19 of 20 questions at a small model's budget (it was 10 of 20), and every lesson was visible on overview questions (it was 2 to 7 of 10).

notes.title: Tagalog lessons
notes.html: Questions are written and checked in the language of your notes, then translated. A translation is only kept if every term and number survives and it means the same when translated back. Models that cannot write reliable Tagalog (such as Qwen2.5-Coder 3B) keep the lesson in your notes' language and tell you so; choose Gemma 3 4B in Settings → AI & Models for Tagalog lessons.

notes.title: New: Math Lab
notes.html:
Next to the Chemistry and Physics Labs on the Study page.

  • Solve: type an equation, a system, "factor …", "derivative of …", "integrate …", two points or a word problem, and see every step worked out and graphed. The math engine computes every answer exactly; the AI only reads word problems and explains on request.
  • Coordinate plane: plot and drag points, see their quadrant, distance, midpoint, slope and the line through them; practice plotting and reading points; connect-the-dots pictures; translations, reflections, rotations and dilations.
  • Functions and graphs: a graphing calculator with sliders and key points (roots, turning points, intersections), lines, parabolas and the unit circle.
  • Algebra, Geometry, Calculus: equations and systems step by step, factor and expand, triangles and circles, derivatives with tangent lines, and area under a curve.

notes.title: Fixes
notes.html: • "Practise mock exam" is now spelled "Practice mock exam".

notes.title: New
notes.html:
• Updates by themselves. When a newer Anvira is published, a small button appears at the top right. Click it to download, then again to restart into the new version. Nothing downloads or restarts until you click. Settings → About → Check for updates looks right now.
  • Runtime updates. A second button appears when a newer Anvira Runtime is available. It updates the AI engine in place; your models and settings are kept.
  • Optional account. Sign in or create an account from the sidebar or Settings → Account. Everything still works without one, and your chats and files stay on your PC.

notes.title: Fixed
notes.html:
• The window now always fits your screen and remembers where you left it (it could hang off the right or bottom edge).
  • The composer "+" menu and dialogs are no longer cut off on small screens.
  • The Search page quick-jump buttons work again.
  • The start-up animation is smoother and the first-run dialog waits for it.
  • Memory recall across chats works.
  • A dropped connection to the AI engine now says what happened ("The AI engine stopped in the middle of the answer") with a hint, instead of a bare "terminated".
  • Very long messages fold up behind Show more so one big paste does not take over the screen.

notes.title: Faster
notes.html:
• The AI serves more than one request at a time. llama-server now runs several slots over one shared context pool: 4 on a GPU with a 16k context, 2 on the processor (whose context grows to 8k for this: a few hundred MB of memory for a small model), 1 when the context is smaller. Chat, Ask AI and ghost text no longer wait behind an exam or lesson being written, and every slot can still use the whole context, so a long prompt never gets less room than before.
  • New setting models.parallel (default: automatic) to choose the number of slots yourself: anvira config set models.parallel 2.
